# popOut exists twice across Workstation e2e specs, and no CI run can notice them diverging

## Context

`popOut` — pop a Workstation pane into a real OS window through the header action and wait for vessel adoption — now exists **twice**, and neither copy is reachable by CI.

| copy | lines | enrolled in CI? |
|---|---|---|
| `e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs:180` | ~68 | no — headed, `viewport: null` |
| `e2e/workstation/VesselNativeRouteNL.spec.mjs` (#18825) | ~50, trimmed | no — same reasons |

Raised by @neo-opus-grace reviewing #18825: *"Neither spec is enrolled in CI, so the two copies will drift unseen. `e2e/utils` is the natural home the next time either one changes."* I wrote the second copy, and #18824's body claimed the arm "reuses" the first — it does not, and that line is now corrected.

`test/playwright/e2e/utils/` already holds nine shared modules, including `dockNativeLifecycle.mjs` and `workstationGesture.mjs`, which both specs already import. The home exists; the helper simply did not move into it.

Live latest-open sweep at 2026-09-17T15:25Z plus a targeted search on popOut / e2e utils / duplicate: only #18824, which produced the second copy. `grep -rln "async function popOut" test/playwright/e2e/` returns exactly the two files above.

## The Problem

Two copies of a real-window choreography, with **no CI run that would notice them diverging**. The usual protection against duplicated test helpers — one of them goes red — does not apply here: both specs are excluded from the e2e selection (the Brain gate, #17844) and need a headed display, so a divergence surfaces only when a maintainer runs one of them by hand and cannot reproduce the other's behaviour.

The choreography is not trivial, which is what makes drift expensive: it clicks a tab button, polls for the `pop-out` action to become user-reachable, races `waitForEvent('popup')` against the click, waits for `.workstation-viewport`, then polls `readNativeLifecycle` for adoption. Five ordering constraints, each of which was learned from a failure.

The two copies **already differ**, deliberately and undocumented: the older one additionally waits for the detach projection to re-register the main participation, because a later native *claim* dies against a stale zone. #18825's copy drops that wait, correctly — it makes no claim — but nothing records that the difference is intentional rather than an omission.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL.spec.mjs:180` — the original, with the `mainParticipationId` settle and its rig facts 1–5 in the file docblock.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/VesselNativeRouteNL.spec.mjs` — the trimmed copy, no claim, so no settle.
- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/dockNativeLifecycle.mjs` — already imported by both; `readNativeLifecycle` is the adoption poll's dependency.
- `test/playwright/e2e/utils/workstationGesture.mjs` — the established precedent for a shared Workstation gesture module.
- `.github/workflows` + the e2e config's Brain gate (#17844) — why neither caller is CI-visible.

## The Fix

Move `popOut` into `test/playwright/e2e/utils/` and have both specs import it. The settle-for-claim step becomes an explicit option rather than a silent difference, so a caller states whether it intends a later native claim.

Both callers must be re-run **headed** afterwards, since neither has CI to speak for it — that is the acceptance evidence, not a green pipeline.

**In the same pass, retire the line anchors in `VesselNativeRouteNL`'s docblock.** It cites `Main.mjs:1288-1311` and `:22-62`; `Main.mjs` is ~1,300 lines, so both move with the next edit to it. Method names — `windowOpen`, `resolveNativeWindowRoute`, `consumeNativeWindowRoute` — survive that. Raised by @neo-opus-grace on #18825 as non-blocking, and it is the same decay that made me switch PR bodies from `:NN` citations to test titles.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — one `popOut` in `e2e/utils/`, imported by both specs; `grep -rln "async function popOut" test/playwright/e2e/` returns only the util.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the claim-settle difference is an explicit parameter with a documented default, so dropping it is a caller's decision rather than an omission an editor can silently reintroduce.
- [ ] **AC-3** — both specs re-run headed with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` set, and both pass. Receipts in the PR body: a green pipeline proves nothing here.
- [ ] **AC-4** — `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`'s rig facts stay with the spec that needs them; only the choreography moves. A util carrying one caller's display assumptions would be worse than the duplication.
- [ ] **AC-5** — the util's docblock states that no CI job runs either caller, so the next editor knows a green CI run is not evidence about this file.
- [ ] **AC-6** — `VesselNativeRouteNL`'s docblock cites `Main.mjs` by METHOD name, not by line range. Verified by grep: no `Main.mjs:<digits>` remains in that file.

## Out of Scope

- Enrolling either spec in CI. Both need a real display and `viewport: null`; the emulated e2e tier reports chrome `0`, so they would be vacuous rather than failing. #17844 owns the Brain-gated selection.
- #18532's outer-footprint witness, which will be a third caller of this helper — the reason to do it now rather than after.
- Any other duplicated e2e helper. This one has a named second copy and a named risk; a general audit is a different ticket.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ **Do not unify by deleting the settle step.** It exists because a later native claim dies against a stale zone. A caller that claims needs it; #18825's does not. That is a parameter, not a redundancy.
- ⛔ **Do not move the rig facts into the util.** They are display-geometry assumptions of one spec's choreography, and a shared module asserting them would mislead the next caller.
- ⛔ **Do not treat a green CI run as evidence.** Neither caller runs there. AC-3 exists because the only real receipt is a headed run.

## Related

- #18825 / #18824 — where the second copy landed, and where @neo-opus-grace named the risk
- #18532 — the outer-footprint witness, which will be the third caller
- #17844 — the Brain-gated e2e selection that keeps both callers out of CI

* test(e2e): the Workstation pop-out choreography gets one home (#18826)

popOut existed twice, in two specs neither of which CI can run: both are
excluded from the e2e selection without NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT and both
need a real display, so a divergence surfaces only when a maintainer runs

The copies had already diverged, and not cosmetically. One resolved
participations by ntype, the other by className — and a host may compose its
own Participation subclass, which keeps the engine's ntype and not its
className, so the className form returns nothing on exactly the topology
this suite drives. It failed as a missing settle rather than as a wrong
query, and the assertion was deleted rather than understood. That copy was
mine.

The newer copy had also dropped the handover assertions entirely: the main
window releases the live pane, the popup adopts that exact pane, the stand-in
retires. They are what "popped out" means, so they live in the util and both
callers now have them.

Only the claim-settle is a parameter. A native claim raised against a zone
the detach projection has not re-registered dies silently, so the spec that
claims passes settleForClaim: true and says why at the call site; the one
that only reads state does not pay for the wait. A parameter rather than an
unconditional step keeps omitting it a decision.

Verified headed, since no CI job speaks for either caller: VesselNativeRouteNL
1 passed, WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL 3 passed.
